2.w: “Listen to my words, you wise men; hear me, you learned men.

3.w: For the ear assesses words as the mouth tastes food.

4.w: Let us evaluate for ourselves what is right; let us come to know among ourselves what is good.

5.w: For Job says, ‘I am innocent, but God turns away my right.

6.w: Concerning my right, should I lie? My wound is incurable, although I am without transgression.’

7.w: Who is there like Job, who drinks derision like water?

8.w: He goes about in company with evildoers; he goes along with wicked men.

9.w: For he says, ‘It does not profit a man when he makes his delight with God.’

10.w: “Therefore, listen to me, you men of understanding. Far be it from God to do wickedness, from the Almighty to do evil.

11.w: For he repays a person for his work, and according to the conduct of a person, he causes the consequences to find him.

12.w: Indeed, in truth, God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.

13.w: Who entrusted to him the earth? And who put him over the whole world?

14.w: If God were to set his heart on it, and gather in his spirit and his breath,

15.w: all flesh would perish together, and human beings would return to dust.

16.w: “If you have understanding, listen to this, hear what I have to say.

17.w: Do you really think that one who hates justice can govern? And will you declare guilty the supremely Righteous One,

18.w: who says to a king, ‘Worthless man,’ and to nobles, ‘Wicked men,’

19.w: who shows no partiality to princes, and does not take note of the rich more than the poor because all of them are the work of his hands?

20.w: In a moment they die, in the middle of the night; people are shaken, and they pass away. The mighty are removed effortlessly.

21.w: For his eyes are on the ways of an individual; he observes all a person’s steps.

22.w: There is no darkness, and no deep darkness, where evildoers can hide themselves.

23.w: For he does not still consider a person, that he should come before God in judgment.

24.w: He shatters the great without inquiry and sets up others in their place.

25.w: Therefore, he knows their deeds; he overthrows them in the night, and they are crushed.

26.w: He strikes them for their wickedness in a place where people can see,

27.w: because they have turned away from following him and have not understood any of his ways,

28.w: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come before him, so that he hears the cry of the needy.

29.w: But if God is quiet, who can condemn him? If he hides his face, then who can see him? Yet he is over the individual and the nation alike,

30.w: so that the godless man should not rule and not lay snares for the people.

31.w: “Has anyone said to God, ‘I have endured chastisement, but I will not act wrongly any more;

32.w: teach me what I cannot see; if I have done evil, I will do so no more’?

33.w: Is it your opinion that God should recompense it, because you reject this? But you must choose, and not I, so tell us what you know.

34.w: Men of understanding say to me— any wise man listening to me says—

35.w: that Job speaks without knowledge and his words are without understanding.

36.w: But Job will be tested to the end, because his answers are like those of wicked men.

37.w: For he adds transgression to his sin; in our midst he claps his hands and multiplies his words against God.”
